changes.old: ### Damage, Destroy, Remove, Replace and Defend
changes.new:
### Damage, Destroy, Remove, Replace and Defend

Use the named operation to determine what happens to the piece:

| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |
| **Replace** | Remove the original piece and put the specified new piece in its place, retaining marked Damage. |

changes.old: Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup.
changes.new: If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees.

changes.old: This post-action-tree correction uses the cleanup procedure below.
changes.new: At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action.
